key_insight: ISLA builds physical symmetries and measure-weighted boundary integration into a transformer to make PDE predictions robust to coordinate changes, units, and boundary resampling.
engineering_relevance: For steady, boundary-driven PDE surrogates, this design reduces sensitivity to object pose and mesh choice while allowing interior query points to be evaluated independently.
method: Use distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors; no learned operation receives coordinates directly.
Normalize lengths by a boundary-derived scale and weight boundary sums by quadrature.
Predict at independent interior queries using a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel.
evidence_signal: On 2,816 AeroZoo flows, mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1× and 3.3× lower than every baseline's, respectively; on AirfRANS, ISLA ranks behind GLOBE.
watch_item: The stated rigid-motion, reflection, unit, and mesh-refinement guarantees require every boundary cell to be a token and an exact boundary read; accelerated approximations merit validation.
paper_title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
